To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the caveolae-dependent pathway of uptake plays a pivotal role in gene transfection in COS-1 cells.
the cellular uptake of polyplex via caveolae plays a pivotal role in gene transfection.
caveolae-mediated endocytosis plays a pivotal role in polyplex-mediated gene delivery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new non-viral gene therapy systems for gene delivery in the brain.
the cellular uptake and intracellular trafficking of non-viral polyplexes and their subsequent gene expression.
the development of a new generation of non-viral vectors that are able to efficiently deliver therapeutic nucleic acids into cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
caveolae are important for efficient gene transfection by non-viral carriers, whereas clathrin-mediated uptake does not seem to be essential.
the caveolae-dependent route of uptake plays a pivotal role in polyplex-mediated gene delivery, whereas the clathrin-mediated uptake route does not.
the caveolae-dependent pathway of uptake is a pivotal route for gene expression, and thus, should be considered in the development of non-viral vectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cellular uptake of pDMAEMA- as well as PEI-DNA polyplexes is mediated by both clathrin- as well as caveolae-mediated endocytosis.
the uptake mechanism of polyplexes is not the rate-limiting step for transfection, but that it is essential for successful gene expression.
caveolae-mediated internalization plays a pivotal role for gene expression in COS 7 cells, whereas uptake via the clatrin-dependent pathway is of minor importance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uptake of cationic polymer-DNA complexes is not dependent upon the presence of a specific receptor, but that caveolae-mediated endocytosis is a pivotal route for efficient gene transfection.
the cellular uptake route of non-viral carriers is not a limiting factor in the efficiency of gene transfection.
the caveolae-dependent uptake route is a crucial factor in gene transfection.
